content.title: Recommendations for fibrinolytic therapy
content.summary: Guideline table summarizing recommendations for use of fibrinolytic therapy, antiplatelet co‑therapy, and anticoagulation co‑therapy in patients for whom fibrinolysis is the reperfusion strategy.

recommendations.recommendation: When fibrinolysis is the reperfusion strategy, initiate treatment as soon as possible after diagnosis in the pre‑hospital setting (aim for target of <10 min to lytic bolus).
Use a fibrin‑specific agent (examples listed: tenecteplase, alteplase, or reteplase).
Consider a half‑dose of tenecteplase in patients >75 years of age.
Anticoagulation is recommended in patients treated with fibrinolysis until revascularization (if performed) or for the duration of hospital stay (up to 8 days).
Enoxaparin i.v. followed by s.c. is recommended as the preferred anticoagulant.
When enoxaparin is not available, unfractionated heparin (UFH) is recommended as a weight‑adjusted i.v. bolus followed by infusion.
In patients treated with streptokinase, an i.v. bolus of fondaparinux followed by an s.c. dose 24 h later should be considered.

content.notes: Abbreviations used on page: i.v. = intravenous; s.c. = subcutaneous; UFH = unfractionated heparin. The table includes citation references supporting each recommendation (not transcribed).
